extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and appellate counsel handling PTAB appeals to the Federal Circuit
extracted.subtask_short: appealing PTAB decisions to Fed. Cir.
extracted.subtask_description: Practical procedural guidance for perfecting and litigating appeals from PTAB final written decisions to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, including deadlines, filing venues, record/appendix rules, briefing schedules, and standards of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to file request for rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing must be filed within 30 days of the date on which the PTAB issued the final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request is not an appeal but asks the PTAB to reconsider matters it 'misapprehended or overlooked.' No prior authorization from the PTAB is required. The request is limited to 15 pages and must 'specifically identify all matters the party believes the Board misapprehended or overlooked, and the place where each matter was previously addressed in a motion, an opposition, or a reply.' The burden of showing a decision should be modified lies with the party challenging the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rehearing request on notice-of-appeal deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If no rehearing is filed, a notice of appeal must be filed within 63 days from the PTAB's final written decision; if a request for rehearing is filed, the 63-day period is stayed until the PTAB acts on the rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rehearing often extends the time for filing an appeal, commonly by about 30 to 45 days (or more) if the PTAB takes that long to decide the rehearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-appeal timing and extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-appeals are controlled by Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(3) and related Federal Circuit rules; if one party timely files a notice of appeal, any other party may file a notice of appeal within 14 days after the first notice was filed or within the time otherwise prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another party files a notice of appeal within the 63-day period but with less than 14 days remaining, the time for any other party to file a cross-appeal will be extended to provide that party at least 14 days to file. This can push out the effective appeal windows for other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to file the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file a notice of appeal with the USPTO director by mailing it to, or serving it by hand upon, the Office of General Counsel of the USPTO; the appellant also must file a copy with the PTAB electronically via the USPTO’s Patent Review Processing System and serve it on each opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneously with filing at the USPTO, the appellant must provide three copies of the notice to the Clerk of the Court for the Federal Circuit, along with the docketing fee (currently $500). The notice must specify the parties taking the appeal, designate the decision(s) being appealed, identify the Federal Circuit as the court to which the appeal is taken, and contain the counsel’s name, current address, and telephone number. The notice should provide sufficient information to allow the USPTO director to determine whether to intervene and typically lists the PTAB decisions and issues on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record on appeal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The record on appeal in a PTAB appeal is limited to: (i) the order involved, (ii) any findings or reports on which the order is based, and (iii) the pleadings, evidence, and other parts of the proceedings before the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before briefing or compiling the appendix, the parties must review the record to determine whether any material previously under seal may be unsealed and must certify compliance with the unsealing review requirement. The USPTO director must transmit to the Federal Circuit a certified list of documents comprising the record within 40 days of receiving a notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to review and address sealed material
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are required to review the record to determine whether any material previously under seal may be unsealed and made public for the appeal, and to certify compliance to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification obligation is mandated by Federal Circuit Rule 11(d) and must be done before briefing or compiling the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of certified record by USPTO director
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 40 days of receiving a notice of appeal, the USPTO director must transmit to the Federal Circuit a certified list of documents comprising the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission by the director triggers docketing and related Federal Circuit deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries of appearance and certificate of interest filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party to the appeal must file entries of appearance and a certificate of interest within two weeks of the date of docketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These filings are triggered by the Federal Circuit’s docketing of the appeal after receiving the certified list from the USPTO director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit briefing schedule (standard appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard briefing proceeds: appellant’s opening brief due within 60 days of docketing; appellee’s response brief due 40 days after the appellant’s brief is served; appellant may serve and file a reply brief within 14 days after service of the appellee’s brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, the appellant must file and serve a joint appendix within seven days after the last reply brief is filed. Parties may seek extensions or request a different briefing schedule; if granted, schedules adjust accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing schedule for cross-appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: In cross-appeal cases, the briefing schedule is extended and includes four briefs instead of three: appellant’s opening brief, cross-appellant’s brief (including response to appellant and its own issues), appellant’s reply (including response to cross-appellant’s issues), and cross-appellant’s reply (due within 14 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page and word limits are somewhat extended to account for the additional issues; timing specifics follow Federal Circuit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint appendix filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file and serve a joint appendix within seven days after the last reply brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint appendix is central to scheduling for oral argument and final disposition; joint appendix filing helps set argument timelines (argument typically within three months of filing the joint appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO right to intervene in appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has a right to intervene in an appeal from a PTAB decision under 35 U.S.C. § 143.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPTO intervenes, the deadline for its brief will generally track the brief of the party it is supporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument practice and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Federal Rules, the Federal Circuit may decline oral argument if the panel unanimously agrees argument is unnecessary, but in practice the court orders argument in all patent cases if requested and available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When held, oral argument typically will be set within three months of the filing of the joint appendix, and parties receive notice approximately six weeks in advance. The court has discretion to decide cases on briefs if argument is unnecessary or if backlog exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical time from docketing to decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit receives the certified list from the USPTO and dockets the appeal, the appeal will generally take between nine and 12 months to reach a decision resolving the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a typical timeline and may vary with extensions, intervenor participation, or court scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing fee and copies requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must provide three copies of the notice of appeal to the Clerk of the Federal Circuit along with the docketing fee; the docketing fee referenced is $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedules may change; follow the court’s current fee schedule and Clerk’s instructions (Fed. Cir. R. 52(a)(3)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of review on appeal from PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal conclusions by the PTAB are reviewed de novo; factual findings are reviewed for substantial evidence; claim construction in IPRs was held to be under the broadest reasonable interpretation at the PTAB (per Cuozzo Speed) but the Federal Circuit reviews factual aspects of claim construction (e.g., extrinsic evidence) for substantial evidence and ultimate claim construction de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cuozzo Speed held that 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) 'prohibits review of the decision to institute IPR' and that the PTAB may apply the broadest reasonable interpretation standard to claim construction for unexpired patents in IPRs. The court cited Teva for the framework: review of underlying factual determinations concerning extrinsic evidence for substantial evidence and ultimate construction de novo. 'Substantial evidence means “such relevant evidence as a reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion.”'

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences from district-court appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from PTAB proceedings differ from district court appeals in several respects, including limited record scope and multiple required filings across USPTO, PTAB, and the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike district-court appeals where notice and fee are filed only in district court, an appellant in PTAB appeals files notices with USPTO, PTAB (electronically), serves opposing parties, and simultaneously supplies copies and fee to the Federal Circuit Clerk. The limited record (orders, findings/reports, pleadings/evidence) constrains what may be argued on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements of the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must specify the party or parties taking the appeal, designate the decision(s) being appealed, identify the Federal Circuit as the court to which the appeal is taken, and contain counsel’s name, current address, and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should provide sufficient information to allow the USPTO director to determine whether to intervene and typically specifies the PTAB decisions that are being appealed as well as listing the issues on appeal.
